parameters.name: Brief-read state (S02 opened; page, clause, sentence, hash per rule)
parameters.relationship: Brief unread -> every badge carries 'brief unread' and cannot turn green. Storing page, clause, sentence and file hash per rule lifts a rule to verified. Paid registration closes 29 Oct 2026.

parameters.name: Tower height H (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip)
parameters.relationship: Height up -> storey count up at fixed floor-to-floor. Pass only inside the band, measured as set in P01-M09. More height raises view-cone and aviation exposure (P01-M04, P01-M05).

parameters.name: Band threshold in the brief's own unit
parameters.relationship: Brief unit is unread. 800-1000 ft = 243.84-304.80 m exactly, against 244-305 m. A tower at 304.9 m passes in metres and fails in feet; 243.9 m the reverse. Those slivers show amber, unit-dependent.

parameters.name: Which towers must lie in the band (all vs at least one)
parameters.relationship: Extract wording (unquoted): one or more towers; REMI says proposals may have one or several towers but gives no band. Default: every tower in band; 'at least one' lets a shorter second tower pass. Ask Buildner.

parameters.name: Counted non-residential floor area (tier chosen)
parameters.relationship: Counted area up -> non-residential FSR up in proportion. Site 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2, so 9.0 FSR needs about 103,213 m2 (derived arithmetic, not a brief figure).

parameters.name: Ledger basis (gross vs zoning)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; the zoning ledger subtracts exclusions, so FSR falls. The brief's basis is unstated: M01 reads one named ledger (default gross) and flags when the two straddle 9.0.

parameters.name: Containment of above-grade volume (encroachment switch)
parameters.relationship: Coverage up -> fewer storeys for the same area but less open ground for public realm. Volume stays inside the block unless the switch allows air-space encroachment over streets, logged as a departure.

parameters.name: Below-grade transit connection: continuity and off-site length
parameters.relationship: Team method: a continuous path from a core to the portal point, crossing under a street outside the polygon if needed. Off-site length up -> walking time and agreements up (MOBI). Station position is unknown until the site plan is read.

parameters.name: Rail tunnel or guideway protection zone and station-connection agreement
parameters.relationship: A path or excavation inside a protection zone may be capped in depth, shoring and levels, and a direct link may need an agreement with the transit owner (reviewer recollection, unopened). Shown unknown until sourced; handed to MOBI and STRC.

parameters.name: Level bands holding public-tagged area
parameters.relationship: More bands with public-tagged area -> closer to the extract's soft aim that public-facing uses reach upward (paraphrase, unquoted). Team preset: 3 bands, editable.

parameters.name: Interpretation switches (height measure; all towers vs one; use tier; ledger)
parameters.relationship: Each switch moves pass/fail without moving the design, so each is logged as an assumption until Buildner answers (Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026).

parameters.name: Submission format rules (boards, size, MB limit, language, anonymity, deadline)
parameters.relationship: Breaking a rule is a submission risk, not a design result. Dates, English, anonymity, team size and no contact with jurors are on the public page; board count, A2 and the MB limit are not (per board or per submission?). Pointer to PRES.

parameters.name: Policy status and version date
parameters.relationship: Newer or under-review documents change which clause applies. Higher Buildings draft policies are due fall 2026-winter 2027, hearing spring 2027, so every result stays provisional until then.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings Figure 1 site list (typed per site)
parameters.relationship: Allowed height differs by site (summaries cite about 700 ft on Georgia, Burrard, Granville; 425-500 ft at bridgeheads; unverified). The City FAQ gives 183 m (600 ft) only for sites across from Bay Parkade. Block lookup runs downstream.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings qualitative criteria (checklist, 6 rows)
parameters.relationship: Excellence with enhanced Urban Design Panel review; public legacy; open space for the plaza network; no adverse microclimate, shadow or view impact; energy leadership; Council approval. People judge them; code never scores them.

parameters.name: Downtown ODP sub-area table (residential_permitted, nonres_fsr_max) by ODP letter
parameters.relationship: The ODP letter selects permitted uses and the non-residential density cap. Area A is pre-filled 'no' from a search summary (unopened, amber). Other letters stay unknown until typed from the PDF.

parameters.name: Open-data label to ODP letter crosswalk
parameters.relationship: Open data has labels A, B, C, C2, E, F, G and others but no C1; the 2009 summary names A, B, C1, F. Wrong pairing moves permitted use and the FSR cap, so C and C2 return unknown until hand-checked.

parameters.name: FSR minimum and maximum, interpretive height, relaxation
parameters.relationship: Cap up -> permitted floor area up; above it, density needs bonus or CD-1 rezoning. ODP height provisions are interpretive and relaxable by the Development Permit Board, so zoning alone does not cap a supertall (summary).

parameters.name: CBD land-use and job-space policy
parameters.relationship: 2009 Metro Core amendments raised non-residential density in Areas A, B, C1 and F and proposed removing residential from C1 and F (search summary, unopened). Whether the 9.0 minimum mirrors it: ask Buildner.

parameters.name: Vehicle parking rule (minimum, maximum, retained minimums)
parameters.relationship: Council removed vehicle parking minimums for all uses citywide in June 2024. Maximum and accessible, visitor, bicycle, loading and passenger-loading minimums are typed. Fewer stalls -> fewer below-grade levels (MOBI), also limited by any rail protection zone.

parameters.name: Transit-oriented area (context only)
parameters.relationship: The provincial rule bars residential parking minimums within 800 m of rapid transit. Vancouver's 2024 rule is wider, so TOA status does not set parking here. Kept as context for provincial minimum-density rules.

parameters.name: Large-sites rezoning policy thresholds (stored values only)
parameters.relationship: Stored: site 8,000 m2 or more OR 45,000 m2 or more of new floor area (search summaries; adopted 25 Jul 2018, effective 1 Sep 2018, amended to Apr 2024). The test against the block runs downstream.

parameters.name: Other rezoning policies likely triggered
parameters.relationship: Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings, public art and bird-friendly guidelines each add submissions and design duties. Reviewer recollection, none opened: unverified register rows (v1).

parameters.name: Reconciliation and UNDRIP register rows
parameters.relationship: City UNDRIP Strategy (2022), City of Reconciliation framework (2014) and Nation engagement in rezonings are unverified rows pointing to CULT, so cultural context is not reduced to view protection. BC DRIPA s.3 opened.

parameters.name: Transit-agency rows: station connection and rail protection zone
parameters.relationship: A direct station link may need a TransLink or BCRTC agreement, and excavation near a tunnel or guideway may be limited (reviewer recollection, unopened). Rows go to MOBI and STRC; below-grade levels may be fewer than parking rules imply.

parameters.name: Zoning path and precedent (outright, relaxation, CD-1; Bay Parkade 27 Jul 2026, 7-3)
parameters.relationship: A CD-1 sets site-specific height, FSR and conditions; Bay Parkade's sets only a maximum height. It shows a path for height beyond policy; it is not a rule and not a program precedent (hotel plus residential, outside the policy area).

parameters.name: Pointer rows: shadow, wind, energy, public views, aviation
parameters.relationship: Rows name the governing documents handed on: shadow and wind comfort (CLIM), energy and emissions (ENER), view cones and airspace nodes in this packet. All unverified until read.

modules.name: Public view-cone checker
modules.effort: L: about 8-12 person-days, all v1: manual-parameter mode and ID crosswalk table 2-3 first; open-data ingestion 3-4; ray-casting 3-5
modules.design_question: Does the massing penetrate a protected public view cone (Queen Elizabeth Park or others), by how much, and does that trigger a Higher Buildings special review?
inputs: Layer0.Massing; highest physical point per tower from P01-M09 in the cone's datum
P01-M09 site_frame: assumed real block, ground elevation, vertical datum
City open data: 24 cone polygons (2D, modified 19 Oct 2026) as the in-force geometry, or cones in the brief package
Crosswalk table of cone IDs, hand-read from the Public Views Guidelines
Cone floors and azimuths typed from the Guidelines, the per-park City view pages (hand-read) or a City View Cone Assessment (views@vancouver.ca)
Brief QE View image: five labelled existing tower heights (S56)
P01-M10 hb_policy_area flag for the block; context massing, optional

parameters.name: Cone lower-boundary elevation at the site
parameters.relationship: Cone floor up -> allowable top up; allowable height = cone floor - ground elevation. Older documents suggest floors near 100-145 m (derived, unverified); 3.2.1 at one West End site about 110.3 m (362 ft), historical and site-specific. Open data has no elevations.

parameters.name: Footprint position relative to the cone polygon
parameters.relationship: Footprint outside the polygon -> no penetration at any height; inside, every metre above the cone floor penetrates. Team check: sampled CBD points fell inside QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.3 (2D, approximate); re-run on the real block.

parameters.name: View origin and subject
parameters.relationship: The origin is the camera for the skyline view; moving it changes every result. The four QEP polygons share a southern apex near 49.242 N (derived). The extract requires one skyline view from the QEP viewpoint.

parameters.name: Cone ID crosswalk and status
parameters.relationship: City data is in force (modified after 10 Jul 2024). 16 of 24 IDs match Storeys directly; 7 differ by suffix (E, G1, G2, J1, J2, 9.2, 20); cone 28 is in neither Storeys list; Storeys 12.2 has no record. Unmatched IDs stay unknown.

parameters.name: Brief QE View reference image
parameters.relationship: Labelled existing towers: Butterfly 179 m, One Wall Centre 150 m, Living Shangri-La 201 m, Royal Centre 141 m, Harbour Centre 147 m. They calibrate the skyline view; they are not cone floors. The VTC band sits about 43-104 m above the tallest (derived).

parameters.name: Higher Buildings site status
parameters.relationship: Only select downtown Higher Buildings sites may enter QEP cone boundaries, through a special review (City page summary, unopened). Elsewhere penetration is not an option. The 2026 review does not revise protected views.

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> allowable height above grade down for a fixed cone floor (arithmetic). Taken from P01-M09 (City 2013 LiDAR DEM or typed).

parameters.name: Highest physical point tested (spire, plant, rig)
parameters.relationship: Rooftop plant, antennae and window-washing rigs count in a cone test, so penetration uses the highest physical point, not the CTBUH architectural top, in the cone's vertical datum.

parameters.name: Angular width of the tower from the origin
parameters.relationship: Width up -> more of the mountain skyline covered. No sourced acceptable-occlusion threshold found (see unresolved relationships).

metrics.name: Maximum penetration per cone
metrics.good: 0 m (all parts outside the cone)
metrics.method: Max over vertices and subdivided edges of (z_highest_point - cone_floor); 'unknown' when no floor is entered.
metrics.basis: Search summary of the Public Views Guidelines: all parts of a building should lie outside cone boundaries. PDF unopened (403 re-tried r3).

metrics.name: Higher Buildings review trigger
metrics.good: no penetration, or penetration only at an identified Higher Buildings site with review planned
metrics.bad: penetration at a site not in the policy area
metrics.method: Penetration > 0 AND hb_policy_area for the block from P01-M10.
metrics.basis: City page summary of the special review; policy area map unopened.

metrics.name: Cone status per cone and ID crosswalk
metrics.good: dataset dated after 10 Jul 2024 (City data, 24 cones) and every ID matched directly or by the hand-read crosswalk; status 'in force per City data'
metrics.bad: ID matched by string guess, an unmatched ID treated as retained, or an eliminated cone tested; 28 and 12.2 stay unknown
metrics.method: Direct match (16), suffix candidates (7) confirmed by hand against the Guidelines, no match (1) flagged unknown; Storeys used for history only.
metrics.basis: Open data opened 21 Oct 2026 (24 records, no elevation field); Storeys lists opened. r1: pre-2024 overstatement claim corrected. r2: ID matching against Storeys fails.

metrics.name: Cone-floor data present

modules.name: Airspace height screening and obstruction marking
modules.effort: S-M: about 4-5 person-days (marking options and checklist 2; optional surface heightfields 2-3)
modules.design_question: Could federal aviation rules (YVR zoning, NAV CANADA procedures, harbour aerodromes) cap tower height, which marking and lighting options apply, and what must the team file or ask?
inputs: Highest physical point per tower, AGL and AMSL, from P01-M09 (roof additions count)
Site latitude/longitude from P01-M09
Typed coordinates: CYHC and the harbour heliport CBC7 (secondary source S65; confirm in the Canada Flight Supplement)
Optional heliport FATO position, approach azimuth, number of paths, performance class
Optional Transport Canada map or surface heights; crane height assumption

parameters.name: Highest physical point, AGL and AMSL
parameters.relationship: Top up -> more likely to penetrate an obstacle surface or instrument procedure and to need NAV CANADA mitigation. A roof mast counts toward height (CAR 601.23(2)). At Bay Parkade, City staff relayed that about 27 m (88 ft) may need cutting.

parameters.name: Obstacle status under CAR 601.23 paragraphs (a)-(e)
parameters.relationship: (d) above 150 m AGL: every VTC tower qualifies, so Standard 621 applies. (b) above 90 m AGL within 6 km of an aerodrome centre. (c) 90 m within 3.7 km of a recognized VFR route. (a) airport surface per TP 312E Ch.4. (e) catenary wires. AGL is not defined there.

parameters.name: Aerodrome status of CYHC and CBC7; VFR routes (601.23(1)(a), (c))
parameters.relationship: (a) needs an airport obstacle limitation surface, which CYHC (described as a registered aerodrome) may not have; (c) needs a VFR route within 3.7 km, unknown until the VFR chart is read. Either would add a trigger, but (d) already applies to every tower.

parameters.name: Distance to CYHC and the harbour heliport (CBC7)
parameters.relationship: Within 6 km, 601.23(1)(b) applies as well as (d). Team-derived: CYHC about 0.8-2.5 km from Area A corners and centroids; CBC7 (Wikipedia coordinates 49.28694 N, 123.10611 W) about 0.7-1.6 km from the Area A ring corners. Aerodrome status unconfirmed.

parameters.name: Configuration A: red (CL-810 steady plus CL-864 flashing), with paint
parameters.relationship: Red lights alone leave daytime paint required (s.4.2(2), s.5.2(1)(b)); on a building paint is a checkerboard (s.3.5(2)) or bands (s.3.5(3)). Consequence: painted crown pattern for SPAC and ECOL. Variant A' (CL-864 only) targets bird fatalities (s.5.4(1)).

parameters.name: Configuration B: medium-intensity white (CL-865), with paint
parameters.relationship: Paint is required above 150 m AGL with this system (s.4.2(3)(b) note, s.6.4(6)); a red-night, medium-white-day dual system too (s.4.2(5)(b)). Strobe-type CL-865 should not be used in urban areas (s.6.2 note): crown carries paint.

parameters.name: Configuration C: high-intensity white (CL-856/857), or dual with high-intensity white, no paint
parameters.relationship: Marking and other lights may be omitted at any height (s.4.2(4)(b), s.4.2(5)(b), s.3.7). May need an environmental evaluation near residences (s.2.4) and glare shielding (s.4.6). Consequence: bare crown, flashing white glare toward neighbours (SPAC, ECOL).

parameters.name: Who decides the final scheme
parameters.relationship: Transport Canada decides. Equivalent marking is approved by the Minister (s.2.1 note, CAR 601.24(2)); shielding only if the regional office assesses it (s.2.2(2)); notice 90 days before construction (s.2.5(1)). An option is a design choice, never an approval.

parameters.name: Distance and bearing to YVR runway strips
parameters.relationship: Under SOR/80-902 approach surfaces rise 1 m per 50 m to 15 km along runway centrelines; outer limits are described mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary. No opened source puts downtown inside: applicability unknown, probably outside.

parameters.name: Proposed 2026 zoning extension
parameters.relationship: The July 2026 consultation adds an area (Vancouver north of the Fraser to English Bay, plus Burnaby) to the April 2024 proposal. Surface type and heights unpublished: if the CBD is inside, a surface may cap towers.

parameters.name: Existing taller buildings under the 2024 proposal
parameters.relationship: In the 2024 text, buildings existing at entry into force become legally non-conforming and may not be raised. The 2026 page is silent on this. Bump-out exceptions were granted in five specific areas, Richmond among them.

parameters.name: Heliport surfaces (operator impact)
parameters.relationship: Standard 325: non-instrument approach 245 m at 6-10%, then 830 m at 16%; transitional 50% to 45 m. A building penetrating them affects the heliport's certification; it is not barred. FATO and class are unknown.

parameters.name: Instrument procedures and harbour water aerodrome (CYHC)
parameters.relationship: NAV CANADA instrument-procedure obstacle clearance and floatplane and helicopter routes near Coal Harbour may bind height more than any zoning surface. Not modelled; named unknowns for NAV CANADA to answer.

parameters.name: Assessment and notice timing
parameters.relationship: NAV CANADA attempts replies in 8-12 weeks; near an airport this can stretch to 12-18 months if mitigations are needed; the letter is not a permit. Transport Canada notice is due 90 days before construction. Late filing risks floor cuts.

metrics.name: Obstacle and notice status (CAR 601.23-601.24, Standard 621 s.2.5)
metrics.good: every tower above 150 m AGL flagged an obstacle under 601.23(1)(d); (a), (b), (c) listed with a state; notice logged at least 90 days before construction
metrics.bad: no notice logged, or notice after design freeze, or (a) or (c) silently omitted
metrics.method: Checklist with dates; obstacle flag true for every tower above 150 m AGL; (b) from the distances; (a) and (c) unknown until sourced.
metrics.basis: CAR 601.23 and 601.24 read directly (601.23(1)(a)-(e) and (2) re-read r3); Standard 621 s.2.5(1) through a summarising fetch.

metrics.bad: 'daytime marking always required above 150 m' applied to every option, or no option recorded

metrics.basis: Verified (CAR 601.23-601.24); r3 critic checked options A, B, C against Standard 621; clause text still to be quoted by the team. r2: 'always required' corrected.

metrics.bad: test skipped, or coordinates not flagged as secondary

metrics.good: <= 0 m, or site outside the outer limits
metrics.method: Optional heightfield: approach 1:50 to 15 km, outer plane 45 m above the reference point (reference 2 m), transitional 1:7. Default state 'outside current zoning (unverified)'.
metrics.basis: Formulas verified in SOR/80-902; applicability to downtown unknown. r1: corrected from verified for this tower.

metrics.good: detailed map obtained and tower top at or below the surface
metrics.bad: top above the surface, or no map (state unknown, grey hatched, never green)
metrics.method: Placeholder until Transport Canada supplies the map (aviation.pac@tc.gc.ca).

metrics.bad: penetration: FLAG for the operator (not a fail); default unknown until FATO and class are entered

metrics.good: display only: marker at 288 m in P01-M08's height ladder, no pass/fail
metrics.bad: not applicable
metrics.method: Marker, not a threshold.
metrics.basis: Daily Hive: possible cut of about 88 ft from 1,034 ft (315 m) to 946 ft (288 m), relayed by City staff; no datum; constraint named only as federal aviation requirements. r1: corrected from a 288 m screening flag.

metrics.good: assessment requested at concept or pre-design stage (usual reply 8-12 weeks)
metrics.bad: requested after design freeze (up to 12-18 months if mitigations are needed near airports)
metrics.method: Checklist date logged by the user; no duration is predicted.

modules.method: 1) Take the highest physical point per tower from P01-M09 (AGL, AMSL). 2) List CAR 601.23 paragraphs per tower: (d) above 150 m AGL; (b) above 90 m AGL within 6 km of an aerodrome centre, with distances to CYHC and CBC7 from typed coordinates; (a) and (c) unknown until sourced. 3) Build the Standard 621 option table A, B, C: paint yes/no, clauses, crown consequence; the user picks per tower; Transport Canada decides. 4) YVR zoning state defaults to outside current zoning (unverified); optional heightfield from user runway data. 5) 2026 surfaces stay unknown until the map arrives. 6) Optional heliport flag from Standard 325 Table 4-1. 7) Checklist: Aeronautical Assessment Form at least 90 days before construction, NAV CANADA portal (separate), map request, crane assumption. Never approved.

Triggers table: CAR 601.23 (a)-(e) with state per tower and source

Map: block, CYHC and CBC7 with 6 km ring and distances

No output is an aviation approval. Jury link: design_excellence_20 (crown, risk, cost of late cuts).

Instrument procedures, CYHC data, VFR routes, heliport certification and the last 33,000 characters of Standard 621 were not read; Appendix C fields not read. Clause details come from a summarising fetch. Screening only.

modules.effort: S: about 2-3 person-days; report-only, no grading until a City guideline is read
modules.design_question: What are the tower positions, floor plates, street walls and separations from on-site and neighbouring existing or approved towers, and which values would need justification once a guideline is read?

Layer0.Podium and site edges (streets, lanes)

parameters.name: Tower-to-tower separation above podium, by use
parameters.relationship: Separation up -> daylight, privacy and sky view up, usable footprint down. A residential candidate of 24.4 m (80 ft) is recalled from Downtown South practice, unverified; office and hotel bands have no known value. Reference line only.

parameters.name: Cross-street separation
parameters.relationship: Towers across a street or lane: separation up with street width, usable plate down. No sourced value; computed from facade normals and reported, not graded.

parameters.name: Floor-plate area and width by level and use
parameters.relationship: Plate width up -> shadow width and wind-facing width up (CLIM packets), slenderness down. A residential candidate near 6,500 sq ft (about 604 m2) is recalled, unverified; no office or hotel cap found. Reference line only.

parameters.name: Street-wall (podium) height and setbacks
parameters.relationship: Podium height up -> stronger street wall and more shelter, less sky view from the street; setback up -> public realm and lane width up, plate area down. No sourced value for Georgia-type streets.

parameters.name: Distance to approved-not-built towers
parameters.relationship: Closer approved towers in the same height range -> separation shrinks and needs negotiation. Context must include approved towers such as Bay Parkade.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north rotation
parameters.relationship: Rotation decides which facade faces which compass direction in sun, wind and energy modules. Read from P01-M09; a default of 0 deg is wrong if the street grid is rotated, so the value comes from the site plan or City street data.

metrics.name: Minimum tower-to-tower separation, residential bands (reference only)
metrics.good: reported; reference line 24.4 m (80 ft), editable; no grade
metrics.bad: no pass or fail until a City guideline is read; office and hotel bands unknown
metrics.method: Minimum polygon distance and facade-normal distance per residential band above podium.
metrics.basis: Recalled residential guideline value; no City guideline could be opened. r2: report-only.

metrics.name: Residential floor-plate area (reference only)
metrics.good: reported; reference line about 604 m2 (6,500 sq ft), editable; no grade
metrics.bad: no pass or fail until a guideline is read
metrics.method: Slab polygon area per residential level.
metrics.basis: Recalled residential practice; not found in an opened source. r2: report-only.

metrics.name: Office and hotel floor-plate band
metrics.good: inside the team-entered band (no default supplied)
metrics.bad: outside the band; unknown when no band is entered
metrics.method: Area per level from slab polygons.
metrics.basis: No sourced downtown floor-plate cap for office or hotel; team setting.

metrics.name: Context completeness
metrics.good: all existing and approved towers within the review radius (editable) are in the model
metrics.bad: any missing
metrics.method: Compare the context list with the City's approved-tower list.
metrics.basis: Brief context includes existing high-rises and approved towers (project extract).

modules.method: Slice each tower into level bands above the podium and tag each band by dominant use. For every tower pair, on-site and context, compute the minimum polygon distance and, for facing facades, the perpendicular distance along facade normals; keep the minimum per band. Compute floor-plate area, perimeter and bounding width per level, plus podium height and setbacks to lot lines and lanes. Compute each facade's grid and true bearing using the P01-M09 rotation. Report values only: recalled residential candidates appear as editable reference lines, never as pass or fail, and office and hotel bands return unknown unless the team enters a band. Return a pair matrix, cross-street distances and closest pairs. Approved-not-built towers are drawn hatched.
visualization: Plan with separation lines labelled in metres and coloured by whether a reference line is set (amber reference, grey none)
Elevation strip showing sky corridors between towers by level band
Floor-plate area bar chart by level and use with the team band shaded
Context towers coloured by status: existing, approved, proposed; approved-not-built drawn hatched
outputs: separation_matrix: pair x band distances, m
floor_plate_table: area, width per level and use
modules.human_judgment: Judging tower rhythm, views between towers and urban-design quality; deciding to depart from a guideline; anticipating the final form of approved neighbours. Jury link: human_scale_40 (sky corridors, daylight, street wall) and design_excellence_20.
modules.limits: No City guideline PDF on tower separation, floor plate or street wall could be opened. 24.4 m and 604 m2 are recalled residential candidates and must not be applied to office or hotel towers. Approved-but-unbuilt towers may change. Shadow, wind and daylight belong to CLIM.

modules.name: Program and FSR accounting
modules.effort: S-M: about 2.5 person-days core (gross ledger by use-group tag, three tiers, reconciliation, stacked bar), browser JS. v1 about 3: zoning ledger, exclusion presets, tornado chart, xlsx export.
modules.design_question: How much floor area counts toward total FSR and the 9.0 non-residential minimum under gross and zoning accounting, and how sensitive is compliance to use tiers, core allocation and exclusions?
inputs: Layer0 program-tagged slab polygons by level (or IFC spaces or mesh volumes, v1), tags in by-law use-group codes
P01-M09 site_area_m2 (gross, optionally net of dedications)
Exclusion preset (editable list with clause ids), v1
Use-tier switch (tiers 1-3) and core/mechanical allocation switch

parameters.name: Accounting basis (gross vs zoning ledger)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; the zoning ledger subtracts listed exclusions, so FSR goes down. The brief's basis is unstated, so both ledgers are shown (zoning in v1) and one is named for P01-M01.

parameters.name: Exclusion rules (example set, v1)
parameters.relationship: Each enabled exclusion -> counted area down -> FSR down. CD-1 by-law examples (site-specific): parking, loading, mechanical at or below base surface; balconies to 8%; amenity to 1,000 m2; storage 3.7 m2 per unit; wall allowance 152 mm.

parameters.name: Use tier for the 9.0 minimum
parameters.relationship: Tier 1 Office; tier 2 adds Retail and Service uses (hotel pending); tier 3 adds Cultural and Recreational, Institutional and non-residential amenity. Residential amenity never counts. Extract wording on uses is unquoted (S02 unopened).

parameters.name: Use-group tags (by-law vocabulary)
parameters.relationship: Layer0 tags carry by-law use-group codes (Office, Retail, Service, Cultural and Recreational, Institutional; others typed when read), so tiers here and the permitted-use lookup share one vocabulary. Untagged area is an error, not zero.

parameters.name: Hotel classification
parameters.relationship: Hotel in tier 2 follows ordinary commercial usage; the by-law is recalled (unverified) to list Hotel under Service Uses. Moving hotel in or out changes FSR by hotel area / site area. Confirm when the by-law is hand-read.

parameters.name: Core, circulation and mechanical allocation
parameters.relationship: Sharing core and mechanical area out to uses by served floor area raises office FSR; separate tags understate it. More mechanical floors -> gross area and height up; exclusions decide whether they count.

parameters.name: Site-area basis
parameters.relationship: Site area down (for example after dedications) -> FSR up for the same floor area. The extract gives only a gross block size; the single value lives in P01-M09.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 1 (office only)
metrics.good: >= 9.0: passes under every reading
metrics.method: Office area / site_area_m2 from P01-M09 on the named ledger.
metrics.basis: 9.0 minimum from the project extract (S02 unopened); tier definitions are team presets.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 2 (office + retail + service incl. hotel; default claim reading)
metrics.method: Tier-2 area, core and mechanical shared out when the switch is on, / site area.
metrics.basis: Extract wording on uses counted is unquoted (S02 unopened). r1: corrected from a strict reading labelled verified, with hotel excluded and core unallocated.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 3 (all non-residential)
metrics.good: >= 9.0 (weakest reading)
metrics.bad: < 9.0: fails under every reading
metrics.method: Adds cultural/recreational, institutional, public and non-residential amenity; residential amenity excluded.
metrics.basis: Wording gap in the extract; team presets.

metrics.name: Interpretation gap (tier 3 minus tier 1)
metrics.good: gap does not change pass/fail
metrics.bad: tier 1 < 9.0 <= tier 3: result depends on interpretation
metrics.method: Three tiers run side by side.
metrics.basis: Wording gap in the extract; ask Buildner.

metrics.name: Total FSR (all uses)
metrics.good: reported only; no overall cap in the extract
metrics.bad: n/a (no cap)
metrics.method: All counted area / site area; Bay Parkade 27.4 (press, consolidated site) for orientation only.
metrics.basis: Extract (unopened); press figure from Storeys (opened).

metrics.name: Use-group tag coverage
metrics.good: 100% of slab area carries a by-law use-group code
metrics.bad: any untagged area
metrics.method: Tagged area / total area per level.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work; code vocabulary named by the round-2 reviewer, by-law unopened.

metrics.name: Ledger reconciliation and exclusion documentation
metrics.good: level totals equal the ledger total, untagged area 0, 100% of exclusions carry a clause id and status
metrics.bad: any mismatch, untagged area or exclusion without a clause
metrics.method: Count documented / total; sum check.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work and sources.

modules.method: Per level and tag, sum slab polygon areas (shoelace formula in browser JS; IfcSpace quantities in v1). Core: gross ledger (all enclosed floor area) by by-law use-group code. v1: zoning ledger (gross minus enabled exclusions, each with a clause id and status). When the switch is on, share core, circulation and mechanical area out to uses by served floor area. Divide by site_area_m2 read from P01-M09. Non-residential FSR for tier 1 (Office), tier 2 (adds Retail and Service uses including hotel) and tier 3 (adds Cultural and Recreational, Institutional, public and non-residential amenity); residential amenity is never counted. v1: one-at-a-time sensitivity on each switch. Reconcile the ledger with level totals; warn on untagged area. CD-1 exclusion values are shown as unverified examples, never as Downtown District rules.
visualization: Stacked bar by level (y = floor, x = m2) coloured by use-group tag
Waterfall: gross GFA -> exclusions -> counted area -> tier 1, 2, 3 non-residential
FSR gauge with the 9.0 line; three tier markers and a ghost marker for the zoning ledger
Tornado chart of FSR change per switch (v1)
outputs: fsr_ledger: level x use-group table, gross (zoning in v1)
allocation_report: core and mechanical shares by use
modules.human_judgment: Classifying mixed or ambiguous spaces; choosing which interpretation to claim; defending exclusions and the hotel classification to the jury; confirming wording with Buildner. Jury link: design_excellence_20 (programme diagram, compliance).

parameters.name: Density above base
parameters.relationship: The Charter allows base density plus higher density when amenities or affordable units are provided, so more extra FSR requested -> more benefit expected. No formula was found.

parameters.name: Form of benefit (five categories)
parameters.relationship: In-kind conditions (s.565(1)(f.1), s.565.17); payment in lieu (s.565.13); DCL (s.523D); ACC (s.523E, in-kind s.523M); negotiated policy CAC (not statutory). An ACC cannot apply where a DCL may be imposed (s.523I(2)).

parameters.name: Free-access floor area given
parameters.relationship: Free-access area up -> benefit up, saleable area down. Bay Parkade secured free resident access to its observation deck by rezoning condition.

parameters.name: Transit entrance and public plaza as benefits
parameters.relationship: Bay Parkade counted new street-level and underground station entrances and a plaza among its benefits, so VTC's below-grade entrance can be logged as a benefit item.

parameters.name: Plan-area contribution expectations
parameters.relationship: The Granville Street Plan (approved 4 Jun 2025) lists a development contribution expectations policy; if the block lies in or near the plan area its terms apply. Text not read.

parameters.name: Large-site policy obligation lines
parameters.relationship: When the resolver says the policy applies, lines open for sustainable site design, green mobility, rainwater, zero waste, low-carbon energy and affordable housing (summary, unverified); a person confirms each. Public art stays a separate recalled line.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings criteria evidence slots
parameters.relationship: Each of the six criteria gets an evidence slot and a named judge (Urban Design Panel, staff, Council). Energy points to ENER, shadow and wind to CLIM. People fill slots; code scores nothing.

parameters.name: Nation partnership and benefits
parameters.relationship: Records of partnership, benefits and engagement with xʷməθkʷəy̓əm, Sḵwx̱wú7mesh and səl̓ilw̓ətaʔɬ are entered only by people and never drafted or scored by the tool. Links to CULT. Sen̓áḵw is a secondary reference.

parameters.relationship: Hotel plus residential, no office, outside the policy area; 27.4 FSR consolidated; storeys differ by source. Fit is height beyond policy, aviation risk and benefit scale, not program or the 9.0 non-residential test.

modules.effort: S: about 1.5 person-days core (typed block, site_area_m2, rotation, ground elevation, datum, height table, convert_height) in browser JS. v1 about 2: sub-area polygon JSON and lookup, City DEM, cone loading.
modules.design_question: Where is the hypothetical block, what are its site area, ground elevation, vertical datum, open-data sub-area label and grid rotation, and how do tower heights convert between brief, CTBUH, view-cone and aviation measures?
inputs: Layer0.Massing with level planes
Assumed block (lat/long or City parcel pick, or a typed local metric polygon), or the brief's site plan and 3D model if they give a location
North-arrow rotation read from the brief's site plan or measured from City street data (deg)
Typed ground elevation, or the City 2013 LiDAR DEM tile (v1)
Station portal point from the brief's site plan
City Downtown District sub-area boundary lines, noded and polygonized offline (v1)

parameters.name: Assumed real location of the block
parameters.relationship: Moving the block along the peninsula changes the sub-area, view cones, airspace distances and ground elevation. Results downstream hold only for the recorded assumption (team assumption until the brief gives a site).

parameters.name: Site area (single value)
parameters.relationship: Site area down (for example after dedications) -> FSR up for the same floor area. Computed once here from the polygon (extract: about 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2) so every consumer reads the same number.

parameters.name: Open-data sub-area label of the block (not an ODP letter)
parameters.relationship: City boundary lines are noded and polygonized offline, then point-in-polygon returns the open-data label with vintage 2020-11-19. Pairing to an ODP letter is a separate hand-checked crosswalk; a wrong label moves permitted use and the FSR cap. Nested rings may be holes.

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower base
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> top elevation above sea level up by the same amount for a fixed height above grade, so allowable height above grade under a cone or surface falls by that amount (arithmetic). City DEM cells are about 1 m.

parameters.name: Vertical datum of each dataset (CGVD28 vs CGVD2013)
parameters.relationship: A datum mismatch shifts every cone and aviation test by the offset: about 0.15-0.2 m near Vancouver (order of magnitude, secondary, unverified). Immaterial for 100 m margins, material near a cone floor: get NRCan GPS-H at the block before any margin under 1 m.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north rotation
parameters.relationship: Rotation up -> every facade bearing shifts by the same angle in sun, wind and energy modules. The value comes from the site plan or City street data; a silent default of 0 deg is wrong if the grid is rotated.

parameters.name: Height measure (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip, highest physical point)
parameters.relationship: Each measure adds or removes rooftop elements: CTBUH architectural top excludes antennae, while aviation height counts roof additions such as a mast (CAR 601.23(2)). Cone and aviation tests therefore use the highest physical point.

parameters.name: Reference level for CTBUH height
parameters.relationship: CTBUH measures from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance. On a sloping downtown block a lower reference entrance -> reported height up by the difference, which can flip the band test.

parameters.name: Ground point that defines AGL for aviation
parameters.relationship: Standard 621 s.4.8(4) treats the tops of adjacent buildings as ground in congested areas, for counting light levels only; CAR 601.23 does not define AGL. Team assumption: the 150 m test uses the lowest adjacent grade (conservative) until Transport Canada confirms.

metrics.name: Height conversion traceability
metrics.good: 100% of heights passed downstream carry measure, datum and ground reference
metrics.bad: any bare number
metrics.method: Type check on every height output.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work; r1 critique found that measures differed between modules.

metrics.name: Site area single source
metrics.good: site_area_m2 computed once here and read by every consumer
metrics.bad: any module recomputes or takes the area from a checker
metrics.method: Lint: no other module outputs site_area_m2.
metrics.basis: r3 critique: a hidden area dependency created an undeclared cycle. Team preset.

metrics.name: Datum recorded
metrics.good: datum named for cone data, DEM and aviation inputs; GPS-H done before any margin under 1 m
metrics.bad: datum unknown: downstream tests return unknown
metrics.method: Required field per dataset.
metrics.basis: City DEM description names the CRS (UTM zone 10, NAD83 CSRS) but no vertical datum; offset about 0.15-0.2 m is secondary.

metrics.name: Grid rotation recorded
metrics.good: rotation entered with source (site plan or City street data)
metrics.bad: default 0 deg used silently
metrics.method: Required field; warns when left at default.
metrics.basis: Value not yet obtained from the brief site plan.

metrics.bad: unknown label: the resolver returns unknown
metrics.method: Noded and polygonized City lines (offline); point-in-polygon at the block centroid.
metrics.basis: Boundary lines opened 21 Oct 2026 (modified 2020-11-19, 29 records, 17 labels); Turf polygonize needs lines that meet only at endpoints; letter-to-designation mapping is in the unopened ODP.

parameters.name: Non-residential FSR cap for the ODP area

flags.claim: The View Protection Guidelines are the governing view policy.
flags.correction: Council replaced them with the Public Views Guidelines on 10 Jul 2024: 38 cones cut to 24, view 3.1 removed, 3.2.1-3.2.4 retained. Use post-2024 geometry.

flags.claim: P01-M02: Sites inside the policy area, buildings up to 600 ft may be considered is a verified, general threshold.
flags.correction: Policy heights are site-specific (Figure 1). 600 ft (183 m) is verified only for the sites immediately across the street from Bay Parkade; elsewhere unverified. A lookup is stored, status unverified until the PDF is read.
flags.detail: City FAQ (opened) ties 600 ft to sites across from Bay Parkade, which itself lies outside the policy area. Summaries of the 2011 and 2018 policy (S08, S09, unopened) give about 700 ft on Georgia/Burrard/Granville and 425-500 ft at bridgeheads. Evidence: S04.

flags.claim: P01-M05: The YVR zoning surface penetration metric is verified for this tower.
flags.correction: Formula verified; applicability to downtown unknown (probably outside current zoning). The July 2026 proposal adds an area to the 2024 one and its surfaces are unpublished.
flags.detail: SOR/80-902 places outer limits mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary. The April 2024 Gazette proposal names Richmond City Centre, Marpole, East Fraser Lands, Big Bend and Delta; downtown is not mentioned. Evidence: S23, S22.

flags.claim: P01-M04: Pre-2024 cone data overstates restriction for the QEP tests.
flags.correction: Record retained, updated or eliminated per cone. QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 are retained; pre-2024 geometry may be unchanged: accept with an unverified, confirm-unchanged badge. Do not test eliminated cones.
flags.detail: Storeys lists QEP views 3.2.1-3.2.4 as retained, none among the 11 updated; only 3.1 and 3.2.4a were eliminated. Global News reports a staff proposal to lower a cone without naming it. Open data holds 24 polygons incl. 3.2.1-3.2.4. Evidence: S14, S15, S45.

flags.claim: P01-M05: The precedent screening flag is 288 m above grade.
flags.correction: 288 m is a display marker labelled measure unstated in the height ladder of P01-M08; it is not a threshold and not on M05's pass/fail cards.
flags.detail: Daily Hive gives 1,034 ft (315 m) with a possible cut of about 88 ft to 946 ft (288 m), attributed to City staff relaying NAV CANADA; no datum, constraint named only as federal aviation requirements. Specific to Bay Parkade. Evidence: S27.

flags.claim: P01-M05: NAV CANADA replies take 12-18 months near airports.
flags.correction: Quote the conditional wording; base the metric on whether a request was logged at concept stage; add the Transport Canada Aeronautical Assessment Form (at least 90 days before construction) as a separate checklist item.
flags.detail: NAV CANADA attempts replies in 8-12 weeks; 12-18 months applies in or around an airport if mitigations are needed. Transport Canada reviews obstacles to be marked and lit; the portal does not connect to it. Evidence: S25.

flags.claim: P01-M01 and P01-M07: The brief rules (244-305 m band, 9.0 non-residential FSR, site size, transit entrance) are verified.

flags.detail: Their only source, S02, is opened=false (email-gated, paid registration). S01 (re-read r3) states dates, organisers, prizes and format basics but no height, FSR, site, transit or board rules. Convention: no verified without an opened source.

flags.claim: P01-M08: Mapping benefits to cash CAC is a verified Vancouver Charter statutory mapping (ss. 565.1, 565.13).
flags.correction: Five categories: in-kind condition (s.565(1)(f.1), s.565.17), payment in lieu (s.565.13), DCL (s.523D), ACC (s.523E, in-kind s.523M), and policy-based CAC (negotiated; policy, unverified).
flags.detail: s.565.1 sets base plus higher density for amenities and s.565.13 allows payment at estimated capital cost; neither sets Vancouver's negotiated rezoning CAC, which follows City policy (unopened). ACCs cannot apply where a DCL may be imposed (s.523I(2)). Evidence: S31, S33.

flags.claim: P01-M08: Bay Parkade is a usable benchmark for a VTC employment-led tower.
flags.correction: Use Bay Parkade only for height beyond policy, aviation risk and benefit scale, with a precedent-fit note. Never for program mix or the 9.0 non-residential test.
flags.detail: Bay Parkade is a hotel tower plus residential and social housing towers, no office, outside the Higher Buildings policy area. Storey counts conflict: Storeys 63, 79, 68; Daily Hive 68 for the hotel; Construction Canada 79. Evidence: S28, S29, S04.

flags.claim: P01-M05 and key findings: Above 150 m AGL daytime marking is always required for every VTC tower, and strobe-type lights are not recommended in urban areas.
flags.correction: Day marking is required above 150 m AGL with red and with medium-intensity white (CL-865) systems, but may be omitted with high-intensity white, or dual systems using high-intensity white, at any height. High-intensity white near residences may need an environmental evaluation and glare shielding. The urban strobe note covers CL-865 units. Transport Canada decides.
flags.detail: Standard 621 s.4.2(3)(b) note, 4.2(4)(b), 4.2(5)(b), 3.7, 6.4(6), 6.2 note, 2.4, 4.6, 2.2, 2.1 note (summarising fetch; clause text still to be quoted). r1 cited s.12.1 for birds; that note concerns wind turbines (building text is s.5.4(1)).
